scope: Static, AI-assisted security review of all 2 changed files (+122/-4), pinned blobs and relevant sampler encoding, binding, capacity, lifetime, mutex and test context. Checked all diff hunks and Unicode. No checkout, import, compilation, tests or source-code execution; no human diff review.
findings: Console aliases are fixed four-word keys; Vulkan samplers are still created from the original layer descriptor. Bit edits stay within that array, and the copied comparison function is range-checked before shifting.

Sampler lookup and insertion use descriptor_mutex, with duplicate detection repeated during insertion. The console-key mutex is released before binding; failed capacity allocation destroys the new sampler, and device teardown owns successful handles.

No malicious pattern found in the full diff and targeted context. The changes add sampler aliases and synthetic test cases, with no new network, process-launch or persistence path. Console encoding accuracy and GPU behavior were not executed or verified.
